newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Part of Credito Argentino stake for sale - paper.
newsitem.headline: Part of Credito Argentino stake for sale - paper.

text.p: Fernando de Santibanes, who owns 28 percent of Banco de Credito Argentino, said he may sell part of the stake, La Nacion newspaper Friday quoted him as saying.
"I think I will sell the securities I bought through financing from the Cairoli family," he said in an interview. La Nacion said that meant half of Santibanes stake.

Credito, one of Argentina's top 10 retail banks, last week signed a deal to sell for $466 million a 71.8 percent of its shares to also local Banco Frances, controlled by Spain's Banco de Bilbao Vizcaya.

According to local media reports, BBV's officials said Frances was in talks to buy Santibanes's stake. "In the case Santibanes sells, we buy and get 100 percent of BC (Credito)," Gonzalo Terrero, in charge of BBV's business in Latin America, said Wednesday according to La Nacion.

BBV's representative Pedro Uriarte told El Cronista newspaper Wednesday that for Santibanes "the decision is as easy as throwing a coin into the air: He sells his stake or he swaps it for Frances's shares and, in that case, he would be left with a nine percent stake in the merged bank."
Santibanes told La Nacion he was planning to sell because he did not want to "have all the eggs in the same basket."
Credito on Thursday reported a net gain of $31.6 million in the first nine months to March 31 versus $13.49 million in the same period a year ago, and a net worth of $305 million.
